parsed.why: Appearance-based prosecutions are current and enforced: trans women jailed five years for clothing (2021), security-force arrests for gender nonconformity (2022), beatings in detention, 'hell' prison, few lawyers. State is perpetrator, not bystander.

Universal entry screening compares appearance to passport sex, with genital X-rays, refusals and deportations across a decade (2013–2025); presentation itself criminalised, with 2017 imprisonment, head-shaving and hormone confiscation. Every trans visitor carries this exposure.

Strong visitor-facing climate: 2012 self-ID law, X markers, courts striking care bans and sentencing a murderer. But record-year hate crimes (2025) and 'desperate' activist testimony show rising hostility; no documented border or facility restriction for visitors.

No criminalisation, but zero recourse: no GI discrimination or hate-crime law, officials exclude trans women from femicide protection, birth-sex prison placement with documented sexual assault, normalised conversion therapy, hostile legislative trajectory, dated violence record.

Same-sex conduct legal, SO discrimination banned, marriage equality since 2025, no facility rules, no criminalisation, no documented visitor friction or targeting. Missing GI-specific coverage is a resident gap; official hostility is dated (2016) social friction, not exposure.
